1.title: Cybersecurity Controls and Professional Conduct
1.text: Welcome to Module four: Cybersecurity Controls and Professional Conduct. It covers the exam area one. Security Principles. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. one point four Understand cybersecurity controls: Technical controls. Administrative controls. Physical controls. one point five Maintain professional and ethical conduct: Professional code of conduct. Due care and due diligence. I S C two Code of Ethics. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: one. Security Principles (twenty-four percent). Exam format: an adaptive exam of one hundred to one hundred twenty-five questions in two hours; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official I S C two C C exam outline.

1.title: Three categories of controls
1.text: Three categories of controls. A control (also called a safeguard or countermeasure) reduces risk.

1.title: Three categories of controls, continued
1.text: Three categories of controls. The figure shows this: Controls by category and by function.

1.title: Three categories of controls, continued
1.text: Three categories of controls. Technical. Also called: Logical. Examples: Firewalls, encryption, access control lists, antivirus, multi-factor authentication, intrusion detection. Administrative. Also called: Managerial or procedural. Examples: Policies, procedures, training, background checks, risk assessments, change management. Physical. Also called: Operational or environmental. Examples: Locks, fences, guards, badges, cameras, fire suppression. Exam tip: Ask what the control is made of. Software or hardware logic equals technical. Rules and people processes equals administrative. Things you can touch in the building equals physical.

1.title: Controls by function
1.text: Controls by function. Preventive. Purpose: Stop the event. Example: Lock, firewall rule, least privilege. Deterrent. Purpose: Discourage the attempt. Example: Warning sign, visible camera, guard. Detective. Purpose: Find the event while or after it happens. Example: Log review, intrusion detection, motion sensor. Corrective. Purpose: Fix the damage and cause. Example: Patching, restoring from backup, quarantining malware.

1.title: Controls by function, continued
1.text: Controls by function. Recovery. Purpose: Return to normal operation. Example: Disaster recovery site, backup restore. Directive. Purpose: Tell people what to do. Example: Policy, procedure, signage. Compensating. Purpose: Replace a control that is not feasible. Example: Extra monitoring when a system cannot be patched. One control can have more than one function: a camera is detective and deterrent. Exam tip: Prevent before the event, detect during, correct after. A compensating control is an alternative that gives similar protection, not an extra layer.

1.title: Professional conduct
1.text: Professional conduct. Cybersecurity professionals have access and trust, so they must follow a professional code of conduct: act legally, honestly and in the interest of the public and the employer, keep skills current and protect confidential information. Due care. Meaning: Doing the right thing: taking reasonable steps to protect assets, the way a prudent person would. Example: Applying patches, training staff. Due diligence. Meaning: Investigating and verifying before acting. Example: Checking a vendor's security before signing. Due diligence is the research; due care is the action. Failing at either can be negligence. Exam tip: Due diligence equals think and check first. Due care equals act and maintain. Remember "diligence equals detective work".

1.title: The ISC2 Code of Ethics
1.text: The I S C two Code of Ethics. The Code has four mandatory canons. They are applied in order: a conflict is settled in favor of the earlier canon. Strict adherence is a condition of the credential; a violation can lead to peer-review action and revocation. one. Protect society, the common good, necessary public trust and confidence, and the infrastructure. two. Act honorably, honestly, justly, responsibly and legally. three. Provide diligent and competent service to principals (employers and clients). four. Advance and protect the profession. Exam tip: Society first, then the law and honor, then the employer, then the profession. If an employer asks for something that harms the public, canon one wins.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A company installs security cameras at all entrances. In which category does this control belong? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Physical, because it protects the building. Cameras at entrances are physical controls; they are detective and deterrent in function.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A firewall rule blocks all inbound traffic to a database server except from the application server. What type of control is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Technical and preventive. A firewall rule is a technical control that stops the event, so it is preventive.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A system cannot be patched because the vendor no longer supports it, so the team adds extra monitoring and isolates it. What are these measures? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Compensating controls that replace the missing patch. When the primary control is not feasible, a compensating control gives similar protection.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Before signing a contract with a cloud provider, a manager reviews the provider's audit reports and security practices. Which concept does this describe? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Due diligence, which means investigating first. Investigating and verifying before acting is due diligence.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A security professional is asked by an employer to hide a data breach that puts the public at risk. Which canon of the I S C two Code of Ethics takes priority? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Protect society, the common good and the infrastructure. The canons are applied in order, so protecting society comes before duty to the employer.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A written procedure for security staff that tells them how to respond to alerts is best described as which function? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Directive, because it tells people what to do. Policies and procedures tell people what to do, which is the directive function.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Name the three control categories. Answer: Technical, administrative and physical. Question two. What is the difference between due care and due diligence? Answer: Due diligence is investigating first; due care is acting to protect. Question three. Which control function discourages an attempt? Answer: Deterrent.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. How many canons does the I S C two Code of Ethics have? Answer: Four. Question five. Which canon comes first? Answer: Protect society, the common good and the infrastructure. Question six. What is a compensating control? Answer: An alternative control used when the usual one is not feasible.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Categories: technical (logical), administrative (managerial), physical. Functions: preventive, deterrent, detective, corrective, recovery, directive, compensating. Due diligence or due care: check first or act and maintain. Code of Ethics: four canons in order: society, honor and law, principals, profession.
